definition: In a complex ion, the ligands raise the energy of some d orbitals of the central ion more than others, so the five d orbitals form two sets separated by an energy gap.
The colour opposite another on the colour wheel; a substance that absorbs one colour of light is seen as its complementary colour.
The number of coordination bonds that ligands form to the central metal ion in a complex, for example 6 in $\ce{[Fe(H2O)6]^2+}$.
